G8800.definition:
1.  placed sideways, slanting, aslant  , Lat.  obliquus , (Thucydides) 
2. πλάγια, ων, τά,  the sides  , (Herdotus Historicus):—;in military sense, τοῖς πλαγίοις ἐπιέναι to attack  the flanks  , (Thucydides); εἰς τὰ πλ. παράγειν or παραπέμπειν to make an army file off  right and left  , (Xenophon Historicus); πλαγίους λαβεῖν τοὺς πολεμίους to take the enemy  in flank  , (Xenophon Historicus) 
3. with Preps. in  adverbial  sense, εἰς πλάγιον  obliquely  , (Xenophon Historicus); εἰς τὰ πλάγια, opposite to εἰς τὸ ἀντίον, (Thucydides); ἐκ πλαγίου  in flank  , (Thucydides); κατὰ πλάγια (Xenophon Historicus) 
4.  metaphorically   not straightforward, crooked, treacherous  , φρένες (Pindar); πλάγια φρονεῖν (Euripides) (ML)

G8801.definition: a making to wander, a dispersing  , τῶν νεῶν (Thucydides) (ML)

G8802.definition:
the oriental plane  , Lat.  platanus , (Aristophanes Comicus) 
From πλατύς, because of its  broad leaves.   (ML)

G8804.definition: mostly, most often, very often  , (Xenophon Historicus), etc. (ML)

G8805.definition: more frequently, oftener  , (Plato Philosophus):  several times, frequently  , (Aristotle Philosopher) (ML)

G8809.definition:
1.  an advantage, gain, privilege  , (Plato Philosophus): in  plural   gains, successes  , (Xenophon Historicus) 
2.  an act of overreaching, selfish trick  , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G8810.definition:
1.  a rib  : mostly in  plural   the ribs, the side  , (Iliad by Homer), etc.;—;also in  singular , (Sophocles Tragicus) 
2. of places, πλευρὸν νεῶν  the side   of the bay where the ships lay, (Sophocles Tragicus); τὸ δεξιὸν πλ. the right  flank   (of an army), (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8811.definition:
a mistake in music, false note  :  metaphorically   a fault, offence, error  , (Plato Philosophus) 
from πλημμελέω (ML)

G8812.definition: to make a false note in music  :  metaphorically   to go wrong, offend, err  , τι in a thing, (Euripides), etc.; εἴς τινα (Aeschines Orator):—;Pass., πλημμελεῖσθαι ὑπό τινος  to be ill-treated   by one, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G8815.definition:
1.  a filling up, filling  , (Plato Philosophus): often of eating and drinking,  satiety  , (Plato Philosophus) 
2.  the completion of a number  , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8816.definition:
1.  near, close to  , with  genitive  or  dative , πλησίοι ἀλλήλων or ἀλλήλοισι (Homer):—; absolute   near, neighbouring  , (Iliad by Homer), etc.:—;as  Substantive   a neighbour  , ἰδὼν ἐς πλ. ἄλλον (Iliad by Homer), etc. 
2.  adverb  πλησίον, doric πλα_τίον, = πέλας,  near, nigh, hard by  , with  genitive , (Homer), etc.; with  dative , (Euripides) 
3. with the Art., ὁ πλησίον (i.e. ὤν);  one's neighbour  , (Theognis Elegiacus), etc.; so in doric, ὁ πλα_τίον (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus):—;also, with  Substantives , ὁ πλ. παράδεισος (Xenophon Historicus) 
4.  comparative  πλησιαίτερος, Sup. -αίτατος, (Xenophon Historicus)—; comparative   adverb  πλησιαιτέρω, (Herdotus Historicus); -αίτερον, (Xenophon Historicus); Sup. -αίτατα, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8818.definition:
1.  to make into bricks  , τὴν γῆν (Herdotus Historicus):—; absolute   to make bricks  , (Aristophanes Comicus);—;so in Mid., thuc. 
2.  to build of brick  , τείχη (Aristophanes Comicus) 
3.  to make in the form of a plinth   or  brick  , (Aristophanes Comicus) 
 (ML)

G8819.definition:
1.  a small brick  , (Thucydides) 
2. = πλαίσιον,  a rectangle   or  square  , (Plutarch) (ML)

G8820.definition: a brick  , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; πλίνθους ἑλκύσαι, εἰρύσαι, Lat.  ducere lateres , to make  bricks  , (Herdotus Historicus); ὀπτᾶν  to bake   them, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8822.definition:
1.  a twining: anything woven, a web  , (Euripides) 
2.  metaphorically   the complication of   a plot, opposite to λύσις, (Aristotle Philosopher) (ML)

G8824.definition:
1.  floating  , (Odyssey by Homer); πλωτοί  swimmers  , i. e. fish, [  variant  dates Anthology Palantina   
2.  navigable  , (Herdotus Historicus) 
3. of seasons,  fit for navigation  , (Polybius Historicus) (ML)

G8827.definition: the organ of   breathing,  the lungs  , Lat.  pulmo , (Iliad by Homer): mostly in  plural , [  variant  dates Tragica Adespota  ; πνεῦμ᾽ ἀνεὶς ἐκ πλευμόνων (Euripides) (ML)

G8828.definition:
1.  grass, herb  , (Homer), etc.; ποία Μηδική, Lat. herba Medica, sainfoin or  lucerne  , (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2.  the grass  , i. e.  a grassy place  , plat., (Xenophon Historicus) 
3. in Poets, of Time, τέσσαρας πόας four  grasses  , i. e.  summers  , [  variant  dates Anthology Palantina   (ML)

G8829.definition:
1.  to long for, yearn after   what is absent,  to miss   or  regret   what is lost, Lat.  desiderare , (Homer), etc.; ποθεῖς τὸν οὐ παρόντα (Aristophanes Comicus); π. τὰς ἐν τῆι νεότητι ἡδονάς (Plato Philosophus):—;Pass., ὦ ποθουμένη (i.e. Εἰρήνη) (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2. of things,  to require  , ποθεῖ ἡ ἀπόκρισις ἐρώτησιν τοιάνδε (Plato Philosophus) 
3. with  infinitive   to be anxious   to do, (Euripides); τὸ νοσοῦν ποθεῖ σε ξυμπαραστάτην λαβεῖν my sickness  needs   to take thee as an assistant, (Sophocles Tragicus) 
4.  absolute , τὸ ποθοῦν  one's desiring, one's longing  , (Sophocles Tragicus) 
5. as Dep., ποθουμένη φρήν the  longing   soul, (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G8830.definition:
1.  a marking with various colours, embroidering, embroidery  , (Plato Philosophus): in  plural   pieces of broidery  , (Xenophon Historicus) 
2.  varied aspect, diversity  , (Plato Philosophus) 
3.  versatility, subtlety, craft  , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G8831.definition:
1.  to work in various colours, to broider, work in embroidery  , (Euripides); χορὸν ποίκιλλε  he wrought a   χορός  of cunning workmanship  , (Iliad by Homer) 
2.  to embroider   a robe, (Pindar), etc. 
3. generally,  to diversify, vary  , (Euripides):—;of style,  to embellish  , (Pindar):—;  to speak as in riddles  , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G8832.definition:
1.  a broidered stuff, brocade  , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
2.  broidered work, broidery  , (Homer) 
3. generally,  a variety, diversity  , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G8837.definition: of   or  for a shepherd  , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus): —; ἡ -κή (i.e. τέχνη); (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G8838.definition:
1.  wool   in its raw state,  a fleece  , (Iliad by Homer), etc.:  a lock   or  tuft of wool  , (Sophocles Tragicus) 
2.  proverbial  in heterocl.  accusative  of 3rd  declension , εἰς ὄνου πόκας to an  ass shearing  , i. e. to no-place, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G8839.definition:
1.  of   or  for war  , (Thucydides); ἀσπὶς πολεμικωτάτη  most fit for service  , (Xenophon Historicus) 
2. ἡ -κή (i.e. τέχνη);  the art of war, war  , (Plato Philosophus): —; τὰ πολεμικά  warlike exercises  , (Thucydides) 
3. τὸ πολεμικόν  the signal for battle  , (Xenophon Historicus) 
4.  the military class  , opposite to the civilian, (Aristotle Philosopher) 
5. of persons,  skilled in war, warlike  , (Thucydides), etc. 
6.  like an enemy, stirring up hostility  , (Xenophon Historicus):—; adverb , πολεμικῶς ἔχειν to be  hostile  , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8840.definition:
1.  of   or  belonging to war  , (Pindar), etc.: —; τὰ πολέμια  whatever belongs to war, war and its business  , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 
2.  of   or  like an enemy, hostile  , (Pindar), etc.:—;as  Substantive   an enemy  , (Herdotus Historicus), attic; οἱ π.  the enemy  , (Thucydides): —; τὸ π.  hostility  , (Thucydides) 
3. generally,  opposed, adverse  , (Herdotus Historicus) 
4.  of   or  from the enemy  , (Aeschulus Tragicus); πολέμια, ων, τά,  enemy's wares, contraband  , (Aristophanes Comicus): —; ἡ πολεμία (i.e. γῆ, χώρα);  the enemy's country  , (Xenophon Historicus) 
5.  adverb  -ίως,  in hostile manner  , (Thucydides) (ML)

G8841.definition:
1.  a warrior, combatant  , (Iliad by Homer), etc. 
2. π. ἵππος  a war-horse, charger  , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

G8843.definition:
1.  to hem in a city, blockade, beleaguer, besiege  , (Herdotus Historicus), attic:—;Pass.  to be besieged, in a state of siege  , (Herdotus Historicus); of Scamander,  to be dammed back  , (Plato Philosophus) 
2.  metaphorically   to be besieged, pestered  , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8844.definition:
1.  a besieging, siege  , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 
2.  metaphorically   a besieging, pestering  , (Plutarch) (ML)

G8845.definition:
1.  gray, grizzled, grisly  , of wolves, of iron, of the sea, (Iliad by Homer) 
2. mostly of hair,  gray   or  hoary   from age, (Homer); πολιοί  gray-haired men  , (Odyssey by Homer), etc.:—; absolute , αἱ πολιαί (i.e. τρίχες); (Pindar); ἅμα ταῖς πολιαῖς κατιούσαις as the  gray hairs   come down (i.e. from the temples to the beard), (Aristophanes Comicus); π. δάκρυον ἐμβαλών  an old man's   tear, (Euripides) 
3.  metaphorically   hoary, venerable  , (Euripides) 
4. like λευκός,  bright, clear, serene  , (Hesiod) (ML)

G8847.definition:
1.  one of many  , Lat.  unus e multis , i.e.  the smallest, least  , (Thucydides), etc.:—;  adverb , δευτέρως καὶ πολλοστῶς  in a very small degree  , (Aristotle Philosopher) 
2. of Time, πολλοστῷ χρόνῳ  after a very long time  , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G8856.definition:
1.  much-tangled, thick-wreathed  , of a serpent's coils, (Euripides); of the polypus,  with tangled, twisting arms  , (Theognis Elegiacus) 
2.  metaphorically   much-twisting, complex, intricate  , [ Refs 5th c.BC ,  5th/4th c.BC ,   variant  dates Anthology Palantina   (ML)

G8860.definition:
1.  long-existing, of olden time, ancient  , (Homeric Hymns) 
2.  lasting for long  , (Aristotle Philosopher):—; comparative  -ώτερος, (Plato Philosophus); Sup. -ώτατος, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8861.definition: to be very careful  , opposite to ὀλιγωρέω, (Aeschines Orator) (ML)

G8862.definition:
1. in early Greek only as Dep. 
2.  absolute   to work hard, do work, suffer toil  , (Homer); περὶ δόρπα πονέοντο  were busied   about their supper, (Iliad by Homer); so, πεπόνητο καθ᾽ ἵππους  was busy   with the horses, of a charioteer, (Iliad by Homer) 
3.  metaphorically   to be in distress, to distress oneself  , (Iliad by Homer):—;  to suffer, be sick  , (Thucydides) 
4. with  accusative   to work hard at, to make   or  do with pains   or  care  , (Homer) 
5. after (Homer), the  active  form prevails 
6.  intransitive   to toil, labour  , (Theognis Elegiacus), attic; μάτην π.  to labour   in vain, (Sophocles Tragicus); with  accusative , τὰ μηδὲν ὠφελοῦντα μὴ πόνει  do   not labour at things that profit not, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
7. with  accusative   cognate , π. πόνον, μόχθους  to go through, suffer   them, [  variant  dates Tragica Adespota  ; also with  accusative  partis, πονεῖν τὰ σκέλη (Aristophanes Comicus) 
8.  absolute   to labour, be hard-pressed, suffer  , (Thucydides):  to be worn out, spoilt  , (Demosthenes Orator) 
9. Pass.,  impersonal , οὐκ ἄλλως αὐτοῖς πεπόνηται = πεπονήκασι, (Plato Philosophus) 
10.  transitive , 
11. with  accusative  pers.  to afflict, distress  , (Pindar):—;Pass.  to be worn out, to suffer greatly  , (Sophocles Tragicus) 
12. Pass., also,  to be trained   or  educated  , (Aristotle Philosopher) 
13. with  accusative  rei, like ἐκπονεῖν,  to gain by toil   or  labour  , χρήματα (Xenophon Historicus): Pass.  to be won   or  achieved by toil  , (Pindar) (ML)

G8863.definition: Dep.  to be evil, act wickedly, play the rogue  , (Aristotle Philosopher); οἱ πεπονηρευμένοι (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G8864.definition:
to pass the sea  , νῆυς ποντοποροῦσα  sea-sailing  , (Odyssey by Homer) 
from ποντοπόρος (ML)

G8866.definition: a house of ill-fame, brothel  , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G8867.definition: of   or  for harlots  , π. τέλος the tax  paid by brothel-keepers  , (Aeschines Orator) (ML)

G8869.definition:
1.  a purple garment   or  covering  , (Xenophon Historicus) 
2.  a red-coloured bird  , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G8874.definition: drinking, a drinking-bout, carousal  , (Xenophon Historicus); παρὰ πότον, Lat.  inter pocula , (Xenophon Historicus); ἐν τοῖς πότοις (Aeschines Orator) (ML)

G8876.definition: a selling, sale  , ὠνῇ τε καὶ πρήσι (ionic  dative ) χρέονται (Herdotus Historicus); ἐπὶ πρήσι for  sale  , (Herdotus Historicus); πρᾶσιν ποιεῖσθαι (Aeschines Orator) (ML)

G8879.definition:
1.  to make soft, mild   or  gentle, to soften, soothe, calm  , (Hesiod), etc.; πρ. ἕλκος  to soothe   a raging sore, (Sophocles Tragicus); πρ. τινὰ λόγοις (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;Pass.  to become soft   or  gentle, grow milder  , (Herdotus Historicus); of passion,  to abate  , (Herdotus Historicus) 
2.  to tame   wild animals, (Hesiod) (ML)

G8880.definition:
1.  a gift of honour  , such as was offered to elders, (Iliad by Homer) 
2.  the privilege of age  , and generally,  a privilege  , (Plato Philosophus), etc. 
3.  the right of the eldest, his share of the inheritance  , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G8881.definition:
1.  an old man  , Lat.  senex , (the prose form is πρεσβύτης); (Sophocles Tragicus):—; ὁ πρέσβυς is used much like ὁ πρεσβύτερος,  the elder  , (Aeschulus Tragicus):—; plural  πρέσβεις,  elders  , always implying dignity,  chiefs, princes  , (Aeschulus Tragicus); epic πρέσβηες (Hesiod) 
2. (Homer) uses only the  comparative  and Sup.,  comparative  πρεσβύτερος, α, ον,  elder, older  , (Iliad by Homer), attic; ἐνιαυτῷ by a year, (Aristophanes Comicus); βουλαὶ πρεσβύτεραι  the wise   councils  of age  , (Pindar);—;Sup. πρεσβύτατος, η, ον,  eldest  , (Iliad by Homer), etc.: —;the  comparative  and Sup. were used of things, πρεσβύτερόν τι (or οὐδὲν); ἔχειν = Lat.  aliquid (or nihil) antiquius habere , to deem  higher, more important  , τὰ τοῦ θεοῦ πρεσβύτερα ποιεῖσθαι ἢ τὰ τῶν ἀνδρῶν (Herdotus Historicus); πρεσβύτατον κρίνειν τι (Thucydides); πρεσβυτέρως γυμναστικὴν μουσικῆς τετιμηκέναι  more highly than . .  , (Plato Philosophus): —;hence, merely of magnitude, πρεσβύτερον κακὸν κακοῦ one evil  greater than   another, (Sophocles Tragicus) 
3. like πρεσβευτής,  an ambassador  , (Aeschulus Tragicus);—; plural  πρέσβεις is more used than πρεσβευταί, (Aristophanes Comicus), etc. 
4.  a chief, president  :  comparative  πρεσβύτερος,  an elder of the Jewish Council  , (New Testament), etc.:  an elder of the Church, presbyter  , (New Testament) (ML)

G8882.definition:
1.  to blow up, swell out by blowing  , ἔπρησεν δ᾽ ἄνεμος μέσον ἱστίον (Odyssey by Homer) 
2.  to blow out, drive out by blowing  , τὸ δ᾽ [ αἷμα] ἀνὰ στόμα πρῆσε he  blew   a shower of blood through his mouth, (Iliad by Homer) (ML)

G8883.definition:
1.  to have   a thing  sold to one, to buy, purchase  , (Homer), attic; with  dative  pretii, πρ. κτεάτεσσιν ἑοῖσιν  to buy with   one's money, (Odyssey by Homer); with  genitive , πρ. θανάτοιο  to purchase by   his death, (Pindar); πρ. τι ταλάντου (Xenophon Historicus); π. πολλοῦ (Xenophon Historicus);  metaphorically , οὐδενὸς λόγου πρίασθαι  to buy at   no price, (Sophocles Tragicus); πρ. τι παρά τινος (Herdotus Historicus):—; πρ. τίμιον τοὔλαιον  to buy   it dear, (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2.  to farm   a tax, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8886.definition:
1.  a choosing   one thing  before   another,  an act of deliberate choice, a purpose, resolution  , (Plato Philosophus), etc.:—; κατὰ προαίρεσιν  on purpose, as one will  , (Aristotle Philosopher) 
2.  a purpose, plan  , or  scope   of action,  a course of life, principle   of action, (Demosthenes Orator) 
3. in political language,  a deliberate course of action, a policy  , (Demosthenes Orator):—;also,  a mode   of government, such as an oligarchy, (Demosthenes Orator); in  plural , τὰς κοινὰς πρ. your public  principles, your general policy  , (Demosthenes Orator) 
4.  a department of government  , (Demosthenes Orator) 
5.  a political party  , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G8890.definition: the space immediately in front of   or  round a town, a suburb  , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. (ML)

G8891.definition: property in cattle   πρόβατα);  cattle  , (Odyssey by Homer) (ML)

G8892.definition:
1.  anything projecting, a headland, promontory  , (Sophocles Tragicus) 
2.  anything put before one, a fence, barrier, screen  , (Herdotus Historicus), attic; πρ. σώματος, of a shield, (Aeschulus Tragicus); προβλήματα ἵππων χαλκᾶ the brasen  armour   of horses, (Xenophon Historicus) 
3. with  genitive   a defence against   a thing, πέτρων (Aeschulus Tragicus); χείματος (Euripides); κακῶν (Aristophanes Comicus) 
4. πρ. φόβου ἢ αἰδοῦς ἔχειν to have fear or shame  as a defence  , (Sophocles Tragicus) 
5.  anything put forward as an excuse   or  screen  , (Demosthenes Orator); so, πρ. λαβεῖν τινά (as we say) to make  a stalking horse   of him, (Sophocles Tragicus) 
6.  that which is proposed, a task, business  , (Euripides) 
7.  a problem   in Geometry, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G8894.definition:
1.  to be ready, willing, eager, zealous to do   a thing, with  infinitive , (Herdotus Historicus), attic; also πρ. ὅπως (Herdotus Historicus), attic 
2.  absolute   to shew zeal, exert oneself  , (Herdotus Historicus):—;  to be of good cheer  , (Xenophon Historicus) 
3. with  accusative  rei,  to be eager   or  zealous for, promote eagerly, desire ardently  , (Thucydides), etc. (ML)

G8895.definition:
1.  the front-door, the door leading from the   αὐλή, (Homer); also in  plural , (Homer) 
2.  the space before a door  , a kind of  porch   or  verandah  , Lat.  vestibulum , (Odyssey by Homer), attic 
3.  metaphorically , Κόρινθος πρόθυρον Ποτειδᾶνος (Pindar); πρόθυρα ἀρετῆς (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G8896.definition:
1.  to send before, send on   or  forward  , (Homer): also,  to send   something  to   another, ἀγγελίας, φήμην (Odyssey by Homer):—; (Homer) often with an  infinitive  added; αἰετὼ προέηκα πέτεσθαι, οὖρον προέηκεν ἀῆναι (Odyssey by Homer) 
2.  to send away, dismiss, let go  , (Iliad by Homer); τήνδε θεῷ πρόες  let   her  go   to the god, i. e. in reverence to him, (Iliad by Homer) 
3.  to let loose, let fall  , especially thoughtlessly, ἔπος προέηκε  let drop   a word, (Odyssey by Homer); πηδάλιον ἐκ χειρῶν προέηκε  he let   the helm  slip   from his hands, (Odyssey by Homer); δάκρυα προῆκεν (Euripides) 
4. of missiles,  to send forth, shoot   or  dart forth  , (Homer) 
5. of a river, ὕδωρ προί̈ει ἐς Πηνειόν  it pours   its water into the Peneius, (Iliad by Homer) 
6. πρ. τινί ποιεῖν τι  to allow   one to do, (Pindar) 
7.  to give up, deliver over, betray   one to his enemy, (Herdotus Historicus): —;Pass.  to be given   or  thrown away  , εἰ προεῖτο ταῦτα (Demosthenes Orator) 
8. ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτίκα ἡδὺ πρ. αὑτόν  to give up   or  devote   oneself to present delights, (Xenophon Historicus) 
9. Mid.  to send forward from oneself, drive forward  , (Xenophon Historicus):—;of sounds,  to utter  , (Aeschines Orator), etc. 
10.  to give up, let go: to give up   to the enemy, (Thucydides), etc.; πρ. σφᾶς αὑτούς  gave   themselves  up as lost  , (Thucydides) 
11.  to desert, abandon  , (Thucydides); οὐδαμῆ προί̈εντο ἑαυτούς  did   not  lose   themselves (i. e. take bribes), (Demosthenes Orator) 
12.  to give away, give freely  , (Thucydides), etc.; προέσθαι ἀπὸ τῶν ἰδίων (Demosthenes Orator) 
13.  to throw off   one's clothes, (Demosthenes Orator): and, in bad sense,  to throw away  , τὸν καιρόν (Demosthenes Orator); τὰ πατρῷα (Aeschines Orator):  absolute   to be lavish  , (Aristotle Philosopher) 
14. a second predicate is sometimes added, ἡμᾶς προέσθαι ἀδικουμένους  to suffer   us to be wronged, (Thucydides); προέμενοι αὐτοὺς ἀπολέσθαι (Xenophon Historicus); πρ. τινὶ ὑμᾶς ἐξαπατῆσαι (Demosthenes Orator) 
15.  to suffer to escape  , (Polybius Historicus) 
16. rarely in good sense,  to give over   to one,  confide to one's care  , (Xenophon Historicus) 
17.  to neglect, disregard  , (Aristotle Philosopher):—;  absolute   to neglect all advice, to be reckless  , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G8897.definition:
1.  to set before;   so in Mid., (Xenophon Historicus) 
2. Pass., with  aorist2   and  perfect   active , φυλακῆς μὴ προκαθεστηκυίας no guard  having been set beforehand  , (Thucydides) (ML)

G8898.definition:
1.  to seize beforehand, preoccupy  , (Thucydides), etc.:—;Pass.  to be preoccupied  , (Thucydides) 
2.  metaphorically   to anticipate, frustrate  , (Thucydides):—;of persons,  to anticipate   or  surprise   them, (Thucydides) 
3.  to overpower before  , (Thucydides) (ML)
